- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast peak heights.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast rise to +3–4% from immediate prior peak.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is trending up, model underestimates continuation; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is flat or neutral (0.3–0.6), model exhibits mean reversion bias; adjust forecast to align with 30-day moving average of history.
- If model forecast is >+2% above recent 10-day high, reduce by 10–20% unless sentiment is strong (≥0.7) and volatility is rising.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >+1.5% from model, check sentiment: if sentiment is rising, model may be too conservative; if falling, model may be overconfident — adjust accordingly.
